title: 45-Day Identification Strategy
name: 45-Day Identification Strategy
metaDescription: How the 45-day identification window works for Phoenix 1031 exchanges, and how investors build a workable candidate list before the clock runs out.

sections.html: The 45-day identification window starts the day your relinquished property closes escrow, not the day you decide to sell. In Phoenix, where industrial and multifamily product turns over fast, that window is the tightest part of the whole exchange, and it does not forgive a slow start.

sections.heading: Why the Window Feels Short in This Market
sections.html:
West Valley industrial space tied to the Loop 303 corridor has been sitting under a few points of vacancy for a while now. Buildings that fit a supply-chain tenant tied to the semiconductor build-out get toured hard and go under contract fast. If you close your relinquished sale on a Friday, you do not get a grace period to shop the Phoenix industrial market before the clock starts running.

Office along Camelback and the Biltmore corridor moves on a different rhythm, but sublease space and smaller floor plates still clear quickly once pricing sets right. Multifamily in Glendale, Peoria, and Tempe draws bids from out-of-state buyers who already know the Phoenix rent comps before your relinquished sale even records. An investor who waits until day 20 to start touring is already behind buyers who have been watching the same Phoenix listings for months.

sections.heading: Building the List Before the Clock Starts
sections.html:
The written identification notice has to reach your qualified intermediary before midnight on day 45, describing each candidate property with a legal description or a street address. Verbal mentions to a broker do not count. A list scratched on a napkin does not count. It has to be signed, dated, and delivered, and the qualified intermediary needs to actually have it in hand, not merely a promise that it is coming.

Investors who get through this window in the Phoenix market without a scramble usually have their homework done before the relinquished sale even closes:

  • Pull comps in the target submarket before day one of the exchange
  • Schedule a lender preflight call for each serious candidate
  • Confirm the qualified intermediary has current wire instructions on file
  • Draft the written identification notice by day 30, not day 44
  • Decide early whether you are counting under the three-property rule or need the 200% rule for a longer list

sections.heading: Common Ways Phoenix Investors Blow the Deadline
sections.html:
The most common miss is treating the identification as informal because the deal feels certain. A broker's verbal confirmation that a warehouse near Goodyear is still available is not a substitute for the written notice your qualified intermediary needs on file. Deals that feel locked up over the phone fall apart in writing more often than investors expect.

The second miss is assuming the calendar bends for weekends or holidays. It does not. Day 45 is day 45 whether it lands on a Tuesday or the day after Thanksgiving. Out-of-state sellers who are slow to sign anything add real risk when there is no slack left in the schedule, and Phoenix has plenty of sellers who are not local and do not feel the same urgency the buyer does.

sections.heading: Where This Fits Into the Larger Exchange
sections.html:
The 45-day window sits inside the larger 180-day exchange period, and both clocks start on the same day. Getting the identification right does not finish the exchange, it just keeps it alive. A clean list on day 45 still has to turn into a closed purchase within the remaining days, and that work should start well before the identification deadline, not after it.

Confirm the specifics of your identification list and the counting rule you are using with your qualified intermediary and tax advisor before you sign anything. The rule you choose early shapes how much flexibility you have later if a candidate property falls through.

sections.heading: A Realistic Day-30 Draft List
sections.html:
A workable draft, ten to fifteen days ahead of the deadline, usually has one front-runner and two backups pulled from different Phoenix submarkets rather than three variations on the same building. A Phoenix investor chasing a West Valley warehouse might pair it with a Camelback office backup and a Tempe multifamily backup, so a single submarket cooling off does not sink the whole list.

By day 30, every name on that draft should already have a lender preflight call scheduled and a comp file started, so the final week is spent confirming details rather than starting from scratch.

faqs.q: What exactly counts as a valid identification under the 45-day rule?
faqs.a: A written notice, signed by the investor and delivered to the qualified intermediary before midnight on day 45, describing each candidate property with a legal description or street address. Verbal identification to a broker or agent does not satisfy the rule, even if the broker later confirms it in an email.

faqs.q: Does the 45-day clock pause for weekends or holidays?
faqs.a: No. The count runs on calendar days from the closing date of the relinquished property, with no extension for weekends, federal holidays, or delays on the buyer's side. Phoenix investors sometimes assume a holiday weekend buys them extra time, and it does not.

faqs.q: Can I change my identification list after I submit it?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as a new written notice is delivered to the qualified intermediary before the 45-day deadline. Nothing submitted after day 45 can be added or substituted, so any changes need to happen with real time to spare.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the 45-day deadline?
faqs.a: The exchange fails and the gain on the relinquished sale becomes taxable in the year of the sale. Confirm the exact deadline calculation with your qualified intermediary and tax advisor as soon as the relinquished property is under contract, not after it closes.

faqs.q: How many properties am I allowed to identify?
faqs.a: It depends on which counting rule applies to your list. Investors identifying three or fewer properties do not need to worry about a value cap; longer lists fall under separate identification rules that should be worked out with your qualified intermediary before day 45.
